card.name: The word reliable before evidence terms
card.fires_on: The word "reliable" (or a similar word such as "Effective") used as an adjective before nouns like data, estimates, studies or method. It often starts a sentence or clause.

modes.label: Reliable before data
modes.description: "Reliable" modifies data, estimates or studies, often with "no" before it.
modes.example: However, there are no<< reliable>> human studies available to support a recommendation for

modes.label: Reliable as a quality
modes.description: "Reliable" appears in a list of qualities, or before a method.
modes.example: A<< reliable>> method of barrier contraception should be used in

modes.label: Section-opening adjective
modes.description: A capitalized quality adjective opens a section or sentence.
modes.example: DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION<< Effective>> dosage of amoxapine may vary

card.writes: It seems to push toward noun words like predictors and predictor, and away from word endings.
card.plain: It fires on the word "reliable" when it describes data, estimates or methods.
